items.title: Developers or renters? The real winners out of affordable housing schemes
items.description: State and federal governments are offering incentives for property developers in exchange for more affordable housing. But a Four Corners investigation has uncovered major flaws in the strategy.

items.title: Exposing illicit tobacco's online marketplace
items.description: The process was simple and the service was speedy but the ease with which 7.30 acquired illicit tobacco products was concerning.

items.title: SMSFs could have to pay victims of financial misconduct
items.description: The assistant treasurer is looking to revamp funding for the Compensation Scheme of Last Resort, saying that large super funds, as well as people with self-managed super funds (SMSFs), could be asked to chip in.

items.title: 'Kill him': Muslim man attacked on way to mosque
items.description: A Muslim man has escaped a near-miss knife attack on his way to evening prayers after police say he was set upon by two men metres away from his local mosque.

items.title: Some women seeking sperm donation are being coerced into sex
items.description: Australia is facing a sperm donation shortage and it is leading those desperate to find a way to conceive down some expensive and potentially dangerous paths.

items.title: Trump wants US to take over Strait of Hormuz and be reimbursed for control
items.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said the only way to restore regular shipping traffic through the strait was to end US military interventions in the waterway.

items.title: UK counter-terrorism police now leading Widdecombe murder investigation
items.description: The counter-terrorism unit has taken charge of the case due to "new information and evidence" on the suspected murder of the former minister, the UK Home Secretary says.

items.title: Jewish staff, students, describe enduring antisemitic jokes and Nazi salutes
items.description: Yasmine Johnson, who is central to the Free Palestine movement across Australian universities, has used her appearance at the royal commission to accuse antisemitism envoy Jillian Segal of "genocide denial".

items.title: Sea World inquest hears crash could have been avoided if pilot looked right
items.description: The chief executive of Sea World Helicopters told a Brisbane inquest he believed pilot Ashley Jenkinson was "totally distracted" by the front row passengers on the joy flight.

items.title: Name revealed of Sydney daycare worker facing 329 alleged child abuse charges
items.description: A Sydney childcare worker faces more than 320 charges over his alleged abuse of 136 children over a 16-year period, as police reveal a list of locations where he worked.

items.title: 'Very irritating, dying. But I'm not afraid of it': Sam Neill seemed unconcerned with death
items.description: Actor Sam Neill might have officially been a Kiwi but he did some of his best work in Australian film and television. At home on either side of the ditch, this is Sam Neill's story.

items.title: How a young doctor ended up being charged with manslaughter after street scuffle
items.description: A young Perth doctor and musician is behind bars, accused of killing a 63-year-old man after a late-night Fremantle scuffle. What do we know?

items.title: Qld's multi-million-dollar family violence prevention cuts 'indefensible'
items.description: The Queensland opposition has labelled the cuts to family and domestic violence funding "indefensible".

items.title: Negotiating your bills could save you thousands. Here's how to start
items.description: Negotiating to reduce your spending and increase your income are tangible ways you can improve your financial situation right now.

items.title: ABC Places quiz: Where in the world are we?
items.description: Your challenge in the ABC Places quiz is to work out the location of 10 photos from around the world. Be warned: we might try to trick you.

items.title: What Elon Musk is getting wrong about The Odyssey
items.description: The tech trillionaire has spent a good chunk of 2026 yelling on X about how Christopher Nolan's adaptation of Homer's Odyssey "desecrates" the ancient poet.

items.title: 'Devoted' Melbourne mother remembered by family after stabbing death
items.description: Lavanya Chappa has been remembered as a devoted mother and dear friend, one week after the mother-of-two was stabbed to death in her Melbourne home.

items.title: How Lindsey Graham's death could affect Donald Trump's agenda
items.description: US senator Lindsey Graham died suddenly on Saturday night, local time, creating an unexpected vacancy in Congress. Here's what we know about what comes next.

items.title: Australian woman was cunning 'Sharia judge' in Syrian camp, ABC told
items.description: Speaking exclusively to the ABC, a security source who dealt directly with Australian woman Hodan Abby calls her a driving force behind many of a Syrian detention camp's problems.

items.title: 'He continues to inspire us': Richard Scolyer's family pay emotional tribute
items.description: Thousands have gathered for Richard Scolyer's state memorial service, with the leading melanoma pathologist remembered as an esteemed researcher and family man.

items.title: Coroner calls for change after man died while paramedic waited outside
items.description: A paramedic who chose not to force entry to a house, despite being told a man was inside and needed medical attention, had "a flawed understanding" of his powers to enter the property, an inquest finds.

items.title: 'Psychopath' Tuchel gives England a chance to prove its mettle
items.description: This England World Cup squad is proving they are different to their predecessors at every stop. Now their manager has just given them their latest challenge.

items.title: Bazball: An uncomplicated idea leaving a very complex legacy
items.description: Brendon McCullum deliberately set out to make England's men's Test team a less complicated team to play cricket for. After four years of Bazball's highs and lows, it leaves a very complicated legacy.

items.title: Sentencing of Molly Ticehurst's killer brought forward
items.description: The sentencing of the man who murdered New South Wales woman Molly Ticehurst has been brought forward to allow a psychiatrist to give evidence.

items.title: Former National Trust director unfairly dismissed, Fair Work Commission finds
items.description: The Fair Work Commission has found Scott Carlin, former managing director of the National Trust of Tasmania, was unfairly dismissed just two months before his two-year contract was set to expire.
